name: treniday
description: Free home workouts that feel like a game, with Goro the gorilla: bodyweight skill branches from wall push-ups to a handstand, yoga and stretching courses, streaks, ranks and achievements. Flutter app for iOS, Android and the web — no ads, no account, all data on the device.

paragraphs: Short bodyweight workouts with Goro the gorilla, from wall push-ups to a handstand.

TreniDay is a home-workout app with a game around it. It guides you from absolute zero (wall push-ups, a first plank, a gentle stretch) to advanced skills (handstand push-ups, L-sit, free handstand, the wheel) through short daily workouts: five courses, each with a host of its own, and courses you put together yourself. Free, with no ads, no subscriptions and no account; everything stays on your device. The iPhone and Android apps are coming to the stores; the web version works today.

Disclaimer This project is developed primarily in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic) — an AI assistant that helps design architecture, write code, and documentation. All technical decisions are reviewed and approved by a human; Claude acts as a co-author, not an autopilot.
features: Smooth progression: reps ↑ → sets ↑ → rest ↓ → a Challenge (judged by Skala the bull) → the next stage; each branch moves on once a day, in any workout

Daily workout generation: the branches take turns day by day; the size is Short, Standard or Full, and the Home button shows an honest time estimate that learns your pace; an arrow on the button unfolds the day's plan

Home screen: before the first workout of the day the host's line, an open challenge to start right there, the next goals (SP to the next rank, the nearest achievement) and the course's branches; after it the latest…

Hands-free workouts: timed holds start after a get-ready countdown (pause if you need more time), holds on one side run on both with a switch-sides countdown, a sound of its own for every moment (all, key only or off)…

Course builder: put a course together from any built-in branches, or make a branch of your own — pick exercises, put them in order, and the app sets the reps, sets, rests and challenges; own courses can be hidden from…
